speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing knee pain after increasing your physical activity. To help me determine the cause, could you tell me exactly where on the knee the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Tear.

Based on your age, the mechanism of injury involving pivoting and twisting during volleyball, and the acute onset of pain, I am highly suspicious of an ACL tear. I will need to confirm this with physical exam maneuvers like the Lachman test and possibly an MRI if you have swelling.
